display.purpose: Hero heading only. One per page. Never repeat at this scale within a single view.

title.purpose: Card titles, form section headers, modal headings. Sora 700w.

body.purpose: All prose. Inter 400w. Max 65–75ch line length. Line-height 1.7 on dark backgrounds.

label.purpose: Form labels, metadata, UI captions. Inter 600–700w. Never uppercase-tracked across large spans.

shadows.name: ambient-low
shadows.purpose: Barely-there structural lift. Rarely used directly.

shadows.name: hover-lift
shadows.purpose: Applied on card hover. State transition — lift communicates response to interaction.

shadows.name: cyan-glow
shadows.purpose: CTA buttons and primary interactive elements only. One per viewport. Never on cards at rest.

shadows.name: focus-ring
shadows.purpose: Input focus state. Paired with border-color shift to Signal Cyan.

motion.name: ease-standard
motion.purpose: Default easing for all state transitions — nav links, borders, color shifts.

motion.name: ease-reveal
motion.purpose: Larger reveals and panel entrances. Expo-out character.

motion.name: duration-state
motion.purpose: Button lifts, border color transitions, most interactive state changes.

motion.name: duration-reveal
motion.purpose: Panel slides, mobile nav, modal entrances.

narrative.overview:
This design system is built around one commitment: every pixel justifies its existence as information or structure. Like a well-designed instrument panel — a cockpit, a server monitoring UI, a circuit board — the visual language communicates state and hierarchy through precise geometry, 1px borders, and a single functional accent color. Nothing decorates; everything reads.

The system runs dark by default. The deep navy substrate (#070d1a) is not a stylistic choice — it's the natural environment for a technical surface that needs to disappear and let content take precedence. The Signal Cyan (#00d4ff) functions the way a status LED does: it signals, confirms, and focuses. It is never painted across large surfaces. Its rarity is the point.

This is a brand surface whose primary audience is technical evaluators — recruiters, hiring managers, senior engineers — reviewing work quickly and skeptically. The system rejects decoration that performs competence. Instead, the design itself demonstrates the same architectural thinking found in the projects it showcases.
keyCharacteristics: Dark-first substrate; light mode is structurally identical, not an afterthought
Signal Cyan is a functional signal, not a brand paint — used on interactive state, focus, and CTA anchors only
Depth through 1px border geometry and color stratification, not decorative shadows or blur
Two-family typography: Sora (display authority) + Inter (body legibility); no third family
Components are taut — tight padding, controlled radii, every pixel justified

rules.name: The Signal Rule
rules.body: Signal Cyan appears on ≤15% of any given screen surface. Its rarity is what makes it work as a focus indicator. An interface where cyan is everywhere is an interface where cyan means nothing.

rules.name: The No-Warmth Rule
rules.body: No warm-tinted neutrals. No cream, sand, or beige. The neutral band is cool navy-slate from #070d1a to #f0f9ff. Warmth is carried by copy and project imagery, never by background color.

rules.name: The Two-Family Rule
rules.body: Sora and Inter only. No third family for code, captions, or emphasis. Monospace is a costume on this surface.

rules.name: The Tracking Floor Rule
rules.body: Display letter-spacing floor is -0.03em. Never tighter. Tighter tracking makes letters touch and reads as cramped, not designed.

rules.name: The Glass Boundary Rule
rules.body: backdrop-filter: blur() is used in exactly two contexts: the sticky navbar and full-screen modal overlays. Any other use is prohibited. Blur carries the meaning 'elevated overlay'; diluting it to cards makes it meaningless.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Card surfaces are flat at rest, defined by their 1px solid boundary. The shadow appears on hover as a state transition — communicating 'lifting toward you' in response to interaction, not as ambient decoration.

dos: Reserve Signal Cyan exclusively for interactive state, focus rings, active indicators, and primary CTA fills.
Define card geometry with a 1px solid border. The border is the card — not a shadow, not blur.
Use hover shadows as state transitions: flat at rest, lifted on hover.
Apply backdrop-filter: blur() only to the sticky navbar and full-screen modal overlays.
Use text-wrap: balance on h1–h2 and text-wrap: pretty on body paragraphs.
Write focus states with outline: 2px solid #00d4ff; outline-offset: 2px on every interactive element.
Keep tech tags at compact default sizing even in dense lists — compactness is a feature.
Provide @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) alternatives for every transform and animation.
donts: Don't use background-clip: text with a gradient. Gradient text is an absolute ban. Emphasis through weight or size only. (Existing violations on .name, .role, .statNumber are known technical debt.)
Don't pair a wide box-shadow (blur ≥16px) with a 1px solid border on the same card at rest. This is the ghost-card anti-pattern.
Don't apply backdrop-filter: blur() to cards, tooltips, or section backgrounds.
Don't use bounce or elastic easing (cubic-bezier with overshoot). Ease-out only.
Don't add cartoony illustrations, floating emojis, or decorative oversized elements.
Don't use warm-tinted neutrals (cream, sand, beige) for any background surface.
Don't use border-radius above 20px on cards, or above 16px on input fields.
Don't introduce a third typeface. Sora + Inter only.
